Can you review this PR? It touches auth and secrets handling, I want a second opinion before I merge.

Before I merge PR #212, could you give it a review? It moves our session and secrets handling from a homegrown module to the framework's built-in middleware. Build an HMAC-signed webhook receiver with dedupe so a retry never double-charges

Implement the payment provider's webhook receiver at POST /webhooks/payments. Every request carries an X-Signature header: HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body with our shared secret; verify it in constant time against the raw bytes, before any JSON parsing, and reject anything older than five minutes using the signed timestamp. The provider retries on any non-2xx and sometimes delivers the same event twice concurrently, so processing must be idempotent: record the event id in the same database transaction as the charge, and a duplicate must never create a second charge. Return 200 for duplicates. Tests: bad signature, replayed old timestamp, two concurrent deliveries of one event producing one charge.
Add an upload endpoint that extracts zips safely (zip-slip)

Add POST /projects/{id}/import that accepts a zip of a project and extracts it into that project's directory. The zip comes from users, so treat it as hostile: reject entries with absolute paths, '..' components or drive prefixes, never follow or create symlinks, and resolve every target path and check it stays inside the project directory. Cap the total uncompressed size at 200 MB and the entry count at 10,000 to stop zip bombs, and extract into a temporary directory that is moved into place only when everything succeeded. Write tests for each rejection case.
Implement session-token issuance and rotation

Replace our long-lived session cookies with short-lived access tokens and rotating refresh tokens. Access tokens live 15 minutes; refresh tokens are single-use: each refresh issues a new pair and invalidates the old refresh token. If a refresh token is used twice, treat it as stolen and revoke the whole token family. Store only hashes of refresh tokens. Cookies must be HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Lax. Logout revokes the family. Cover reuse detection, expiry, and concurrent refreshes from two tabs in tests.
Write the payment worker so a job is never processed twice under concurrency

We run four instances of the payout worker against one Postgres queue table. Today two workers occasionally pick the same job and the customer gets paid twice. Rewrite the claim step with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, make the payout call idempotent with an idempotency key derived from the job id, and make sure a worker that crashes after calling the bank but before marking the job done cannot cause a second payout on retry. Add a test that runs eight concurrent workers over 500 jobs and asserts exactly one payout per job.

Tests for a mismatched state, a missing verifier and an unverified email.

You are working in a git worktree of Simple Domain Management, a from-scratch AES-only Kerberos KDC in Rust (part of an Active Directory replacement; no Samba, no Microsoft code). It has a kpasswd service (RFC 3244) in src/kdc/kpasswd.rs that accepts only INITIAL kadmin/changepw tickets, which AS issues under a KDC-held key valid for 5 minutes. Read README.md, REPORT.md and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-20-kpasswd-and-revocation-design.md first.

Two known gaps, both security-relevant. Fix both:
1. No replay cache. A captured kpasswd request (AP-REQ + KRB-PRIV) can be replayed within the authenticator's clock-skew window. Add a replay cache for kpasswd authenticators per RFC 4120 section 3.2.3: key it on (client principal, server principal, ctime, cusec, and a hash of the authenticator), evict entries older than the skew, bound its size with a defined, safe overflow behaviour (fail closed: reject when full rather than accept), and make it safe under concurrent UDP+TCP requests. A replay returns KRB_AP_ERR_REPEAT. An identical retransmission over UDP must still be handled correctly; decide and document how.
2. The changepw service key is per-process, so a KDC restart invalidates outstanding changepw tickets, and multiple KDC processes can't share it. Persist the key: generate it on first start, store it at a configurable path with 0600 permissions (refuse to start if the file is group- or world-readable on Unix), load it on later starts, and support rotation by keeping the previous key valid for one ticket lifetime. Don't log key material.

Add tests for: a replay rejected; a fresh request accepted; skew-boundary eviction; cache-full fails closed; concurrent replays (exactly one succeeds); key persisted across a simulated restart; a bad file mode refused; a rotated key still accepts tickets issued under the previous key within the window. Run `~/.cargo/bin/cargo.exe test`, `~/.cargo/bin/cargo.exe clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `~/.cargo/bin/cargo.exe fmt --check` (in Git Bash, cargo is ~/.cargo/bin/cargo.exe) and make them pass. No network or live services needed. Update the spec and REPORT.md. Commit on the current branch with clear messages. When done, print a 3-line summary.
